content.text:
Salt-wind walks the shingle every dawn,
and the sea unfolds its slow, grey hands,
gathering the stones it has not yet drawn
back into the deep where the old tide stands.

It keeps no ledger of the ships it bore,
nor of the names the drowned gave up to foam.
It only breathes, and breathes, and comes once more,
a patient mouth that has forgotten home.

Beneath the hull of light, a country lies
of kelp-forests swaying in their sleep,
where silver shoals wheel through the dim blue skies
that only fish and lantern-eyed things keep.

The gulls cry out their small, sharp songs,
and the waves reply in their long, low tongue,
a hymn with no beginning and no wrongs,
sung by the water, to the wind, unsung.

At evening, the horizon bleeds to rose,
and the moon pulls at the water like a thread,
lifting each wave in silver as it goes,
until the whole dark world is softly spread.

So let the sea keep what it will take,
the wreck, the shell, the sorrow, and the sand.
It gives us back the light for our own sake,
and bids us stand and watch, and understand.
